naming_derivation: REPOSITORY-NATIVE, MEASURED. The companion-amendment convention is <BASE_PACKAGE>_AMENDMENT_v1.0.N.json in the base package's own directory, with N starting at 1: docs/ops/wave2/W2_B5_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json -> W2_B5_AUTHORITY_AMENDMENT_v1.0.2.json, and docs/ops/p1a/P1A_FULL_BOOTSTRAP_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json -> P1A_FULL_BOOTSTRAP_AUTHORITY_AMENDMENT_v1.0.1.json and _v1.0.2.json. `git grep -l MULTI_ORG_S1_S2_EXECUTION_SCOPE_AUTHORITY_AMENDMENT` returns ZERO occurrences across every reachable commit, so v1.0.1 is the first amendment of this package.
purpose: Carry the execution-scope half of the S1/S2 successor authority: the FINAL path ceilings for both lanes after the repairs in the companion ODS addendum, the exact route-topology regression S2 must install, the parallelism proof, and the S1 product semantics that remain frozen verbatim. It changes no product code, no schema and no test.
scope_note: AMENDS BY ADDITION ONLY. Every grant, prohibition, product semantic and security invariant frozen by MULTI_ORG_S1_S2_EXECUTION_SCOPE_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json remains in force byte-unchanged. This amendment adds the paths that document provably could not be exercised without, corrects one measurement gap in its companion's migration reasoning, and restates the frozen semantics so an implementing mission needs no third artifact. It reopens no adjudicated product decision.

delta_from_v1_0_0.unchanged: All six paths the base authority granted are retained verbatim.

S1_LANE.invocation: pnpm ods:scope -- --base <INTEGRATION_SHA> --protected-authority HPO-ODS-W2-20 --protected-authority HPO-ODS-W2-21 --allow <each path above, exactly>
S1_LANE.multiple_grants_are_supported: MACHINE-PROVEN at INTEGRATION_SHA in scripts/ods-scope.ts, three independent ways: the usage banner documents '[--protected-authority <id> ...]'; the header records that the flag 'MAY be repeated. Every occurrence is resolved ... independently' and that an unresolved id 'never broadens, narrows, or invalidates what any OTHER supplied id resolved'; and resolveProtectedGrants takes authorityIds: string[], maps each through the singular resolver, and classifyPaths unions the resolved pattern sets with .some(). Passing two ids is not an extension of the gate - it is its documented contract.
S1_LANE.ceiling_semantics: A CEILING resolved by ods:scope against the lane's own --allow list, never a mandate. A lane may change a SUBSET. A path outside the list fails closed. A resolved grant authorizes a protected path ONLY together with an ordinary --allow entry covering the same path; both remain mandatory.

delta_from_v1_0_0.unchanged: All five paths the base authority granted are retained verbatim.

S2_ROUTE_TOPOLOGY_DECISION.RATIFIED: The selected-organization selector remains an explicit PRE-ORGANIZATION route at app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/select/*.
S2_ROUTE_TOPOLOGY_DECISION.not_relocated: It is NOT moved beneath app/app/**. Requiring organization scope in order to reach the organization selector is circular: app/app/layout.tsx calls requireOrganizationAccess(), which redirects a user without an organization to onboarding, so a selector placed there could never be reached by the only users who need it. This is the same cycle closed historically by commit 65ab17d.
S2_ROUTE_TOPOLOGY_DECISION.the_regression_evolves_deliberately: The existing route-security control is made STRICTER rather than widened. Widening is the failure mode this decision exists to avoid.
S2_ROUTE_TOPOLOGY_DECISION.control_replaced: The control currently at :155, 'carves out EXACTLY one route - every other /app/* page stays gated', whose sweep at :167 reads only the FIRST level of directory names beneath each app/(group)/app/ and asserts ['onboarding'] at :172.
S2_ROUTE_TOPOLOGY_DECISION.why_it_must_change: MECHANICAL, NOT DISCRETIONARY. Creating app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/select/page.tsx makes the swept set ['onboarding','organizations'], which fails the exact-equality assertion. S2 cannot land without touching this control.

EXACT_RULE_AUTHORIZED.shape: RECURSIVE ROUTE-PATH ENUMERATION. For each route group directory app/(<group>)/, if app/(<group>)/app/ exists, walk it recursively; every directory containing a route-serving file contributes its path RELATIVE to that app/ root, joined with '/'. Assert the deduplicated sorted set equals the exact declared carve-out list.
EXACT_RULE_AUTHORIZED.route_file_measurement_obligation: BINDING. The S2 mission MUST re-measure the repository's actual route-file conventions at its own head and use the set it measures. Omitting a name the repository DOES use would silently un-gate a route - the precise failure this control exists to prevent. Including a name it does not use is inert. MEASURED at INTEGRATION_SHA: the only route-serving file beneath any app/(group)/app/ tree is app/(authenticated)/app/onboarding/page.tsx.
EXACT_RULE_AUTHORIZED.explicitly_not_authorized: ['onboarding','organizations']. A top-level-directory form would silently authorize EVERY future app/(authenticated)/app/organizations/** route - create, [id], settings and any successor - none of which has been adjudicated as a pre-organization surface. This is expectation broadening, which the ODS existing-test adjustment class forbids.

BINDING_STRICTNESS_PROOF.obligation: The replacement must be proven STRICTLY STRONGER than the control it replaces, in both directions, BEFORE it is accepted. A replacement that is merely DIFFERENT, or that trades one blind spot for another, is gate weakening and is a STOP.

required_rows.significance: IDENTICAL VERDICT. Proves the replacement is not repairing a currently-failing control and introduces no regression on today's tree.
The authorized carve-out, and only it, is admitted.

required_rows.new_control: FAIL - 'organizations/create' is not a declared carve-out
required_rows.significance: THE LOAD-BEARING ROW. This is exactly the future route the forbidden widening would have silently authorized.

required_rows.new_control: FAIL - 'organizations/[id]' is not a declared carve-out
required_rows.significance: Dynamic segments are caught identically; the rule is path-shaped, not name-shaped.

required_rows.old_control: PASS - reports only the top-level name 'onboarding'
required_rows.new_control: FAIL - 'onboarding/step2' is not a declared carve-out
required_rows.significance: CLOSES A PRE-EXISTING BLIND SPOT. The CURRENT control cannot see a nested ungated route at all. The replacement is therefore strictly stronger even on a surface unrelated to S2, which is independent evidence that this is a strengthening and not an accommodation.

BINDING_STRICTNESS_PROOF.non_vacuity: Each mutation row must be produced by actually creating the file and observing the failure, or by driving the enumeration function over a fixture tree that contains it. Asserting the rows from reasoning alone is not a proof.

MIRRORED_NEGATIVE_CONTROL_AUTHORIZED.message: the organization selector is back inside the organisation-gated layout - the circular gate
MIRRORED_NEGATIVE_CONTROL_AUTHORIZED.precedent: Mechanically identical to the existing onboarding old-location control at :135, whose comment reads 'The old location. Its return would reinstate the cycle verbatim.'

SINGULAR_PLURAL_CONFLATION_HAZARD.measured: app/app/organization/ (SINGULAR) exists at INTEGRATION_SHA and is legitimately organization-gated; the sibling control at :180 already names 'organization' among the routes that must stay gated. S2 introduces 'organizations' (PLURAL) as a pre-organization carve-out.
SINGULAR_PLURAL_CONFLATION_HAZARD.why_it_is_material: The two paths differ by one character and sit one directory apart. A grep, a rename, an autocomplete or a hurried review can substitute one for the other, and doing so would either un-gate the organization workspace or re-gate the selector into the circular state.
SINGULAR_PLURAL_CONFLATION_HAZARD.obligation: BOTH halves must be asserted in the same file: the SINGULAR app/app/organization/ stays inside the organization gate, and the PLURAL organizations/select is the ONLY ungated member of its subtree.
SINGULAR_PLURAL_CONFLATION_HAZARD.out_of_scope_recorded_affirmatively: app/admin/organizations exists but lies OUTSIDE every app/(group)/app/ tree, so the recursive sweep never reaches it. It is neither granted nor implicated by this carve-out doctrine. Recorded explicitly so a future reader does not 'fix' the sweep to include it and thereby import an admin surface into a tenancy decision.

S2_ROUTE_TOPOLOGY_DECISION.sibling_controls_frozen: The three other controls in the same describe block - the onboarding old-location control, the (authenticated)-layout-does-not-gate control, and the workspace-routes-still-gated control - are NOT authorized for change. Only the exact-carve-out control is replaced, and the mirrored negative control is added.

BACKFILL_FOUNDED_BY.rule: Historical organizations.founded_by may be populated ONLY where there is EXACTLY ONE qualifying 'organization.created' audit row with a non-null actor.
BACKFILL_FOUNDED_BY.anchor_verified: The audit action constant exists at lib/audit/logger.ts - ORGANIZATION_CREATED: 'organization.created'. The rule binds to a real object, not a hoped-for one.

BACKFILL_PROVENANCE.rule: founding_provenance = 'unknown' for ALL historical backfilled rows, unconditionally.
BACKFILL_PROVENANCE.prohibition: Never infer self_service provenance from code-history uniqueness. A single historical creation path in the codebase is evidence about the CODE, not about how any particular row came to exist.

LIVE_DATA_ROLE.rule: Live database measurement establishes COVERAGE ONLY - how many rows received a non-null founded_by.
LIVE_DATA_ROLE.prohibition: It cannot upgrade historical provenance classification. A 100 percent coverage measurement is not evidence of self_service provenance for any row.

BOOTSTRAP_RLS_WALL.rule: S1 does NOT solve self-service bootstrap/RLS. That wall is pre-existing and remains exactly where it is.
BOOTSTRAP_RLS_WALL.elevated_identity_is_valid: Elevated PostgreSQL identity is valid for proving S1's DB invariants - founder cardinality, the FK, the provenance discriminator domain and backfill determinism.
BOOTSTRAP_RLS_WALL.s3_remains_ungranted: db/identity-context.ts, lib/auth/database-context.ts, lib/auth/session.ts, lib/auth/permissions.ts and lib/auth/roles.ts are NOT in either lane's ceiling. Stated affirmatively because making the S2 carrier useful invites reading it in exactly those files, which would be S3 performed without S3's lineage.

ORDINARY_USER_NEGATIVE_CONTROL.what_it_must_prove: That S1 did NOT accidentally weaken the pre-existing bootstrap/RLS wall.
ORDINARY_USER_NEGATIVE_CONTROL.the_vacuity_hazard: MEASURED AND CONCRETE. An ordinary-role INSERT INTO organizations can fail at three different walls, and a bare rejects assertion cannot tell them apart.

walls.42501_or_rls_policy_violation: THE BOOTSTRAP WALL - the one this control must prove intact. CORRECT.
walls.23502_not_null_violation_on_founded_by: S1's OWN new column. WRONG WALL - the control is vacuous.
walls.23503_foreign_key_violation_on_founded_b: S1's OWN new FK. WRONG WALL - the control is vacuous.

ORDINARY_USER_NEGATIVE_CONTROL.BINDING_FORM: Assert POSITIVELY that the failure SQLSTATE is the permission/RLS class (42501, or the RLS policy-violation class the driver surfaces), AND assert NEGATIVELY that it is neither 23502 nor 23503.
ORDINARY_USER_NEGATIVE_CONTROL.declaration_obligation: The test title AND an in-file comment must state that it proves the PRE-EXISTING RLS/bootstrap wall, NOT S1's new constraints. A control that passes because S1's own NOT NULL fired first would prove the wall intact only by accident, and would keep passing if the RLS wall were later deleted.
